Zoom in: the mechanisms inside the boxes
Embeddings carry no word order — a transformer sees a set of tokens, not a sequence. A positional encoding (a
vector standing for each slot’s position) is added to every token embedding, so the model can tell
How a plain embedding becomes context-aware. Each token compares itself against every other token, gets a
relevance weight for each, then takes a weighted sum of their information. The output is a context vector:
“bank” beside “river” ends up different from “bank” beside “money.” Every token does this at once — the
encoder’s parallelism, and the “self-attention + feed-forward” line in box 3’s code.
The output layer emits one raw score (a logit) per vocabulary token. Softmax squashes those scores into
probabilities that sum to 1, so the largest is the model’s pick — exactly your MNIST final layer, just with
The encoder’s output (box 4) is not copied into the decoder — it is attended to. Every decoder block runs two
attention steps: (1) self-attention over the tokens generated so far (“what have I written?”), then
(2) cross-attention, where the decoder forms the queries and the encoder’s output supplies the keys and values
(“what in the source matters right now?”). So at each step the decoder re-reads the whole input sentence and
blends it with what it has produced. That single arrow from 4 to 7 is this cross-attention link.
Where each half became a real model family
Masks random words and fills them back in; sees the whole
sentence both ways at once. Good for understanding.
Predicts the next word from left context only; generates one
token at a time (the loop in 5–9). Good for generating.
